title: A readable diff for a crew roster

blocks.text: A utility's line-maintenance group assigns jobs to crews with a model that minimizes cost, and keeps golden records of a few rosters. Their regression test compares records with `==` and fails with a screen of nested dictionaries whenever anything moves, including the last digits of a float. Write the comparison that replaces it.

The docstring of `roster_golden.py` gives a record's shape, and `TOLERANCE` gives what "the same" means for each float field, in that field's own units: $1 for cost, 0.01 hours for overtime. Write `compare(expected, actual)`, returning one line per difference, in this order and format:

items: if the status differs, only `status: <old> -> <new>`, and nothing else, because a roster that did not solve cannot be compared field by field;
`cost: <old> -> <new>`, both with two decimals, if the costs differ by more than the tolerance;
for each job in either record, in sorted order, `assign: <job> <old crew> -> <new crew>` if its crew differs, writing `none` for a record that does not assign it;
for each crew in either record, in sorted order, `overtime <crew>: <old> -> <new>`, two decimals, if the hours differ by more than the tolerance; a crew a record does not list has 0 hours.

blocks.text: An identical record gives an empty list. About fifteen lines.

"""Compare a crew-roster result with its golden record.

A record is a dict:
    "status":   the solver's termination, e.g. "OPTIMAL"
    "cost":     the roster's cost in dollars (a float from the solver)
    "assign":   {job: crew}
    "overtime": {crew: overtime hours} (floats from the solver; a crew not listed has 0)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

TOLERANCE = {"cost": 1.0, "overtime": 0.01}   # $1 on cost; 0.01 hours (36 seconds) on overtime

    return []

if __name__ == "__main__":
    golden = {"status": "OPTIMAL", "cost": 1200.0, "assign": {"j1": "red"}, "overtime": {"red": 2.0}}
    print(compare(golden, {**golden, "cost": 1250.0}))

cases.says: an identical record gives no lines, and one with a new cost and a job on another crew gives exactly those two lines
a cost that differs by solver noise is the same cost, and one that differs by more than $1 is not
a job the new roster assigns and the golden one did not is reported as well as one it dropped
overtime of 0 against 0.004 hours is the same, since the tolerance is in hours, not a share of the value
when the status changed, that is the only line, since the rest cannot be compared
